chunks: And ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a mukātab who died while having wealth, and he said: His wealth is to be reckoned in proportion to the part of him that had been freed for his heirs, and in proportion to the part that had not been freed it is to be reckoned for his masters who made the contract with him, from his wealth.

key_terms.كَاتَبُوهُ: They entered into a manumission contract with him.
key_terms.لِأَرْبَابِهِ: For his masters who retain ownership over the unfreed portion.
key_terms.لِوَرَثَتِهِ: For his legal heirs who inherit his estate.
key_terms.مَالٌ: Property or wealth left by the deceased.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave under a contractual arrangement to purchase his freedom.

ai.seo_question: How is the wealth of a mukātab divided if he dies before completing his contract of freedom?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the estate of a mukātab, a slave under a contract of emancipation, if he dies before full manumission. His wealth is apportioned according to the degree of freedom already attained: the freed portion goes to his heirs, while the unfreed portion belongs to his masters.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5742 - Asim ibn Humaid narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said: "

The Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled regarding a mukatab (a slave under a contract for freedom) who died and had wealth.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: 'His wealth should be divided in proportion to what part of him had been freed for his heirs, and the portion that was not yet freed should be calculated for his masters who had entered into the contract with him from his wealth.'"
